correctness.rationale: Starting from the primary source equation (34), the quarter-flux identity converts the magnetic factor to \(-\tfrac12\cos(2\pi k)\). For coprime \(p,q\), normalization reduces the density to the sign measure of \(-\cos((p+q)t)\sin(pt)\sin(qt)\). Exact floor-parity algebra and a residue permutation modulo \(p+q\) give the counting function \(N(x)=p+q-1-\lfloor px\rfloor-\lfloor qx\rfloor\); integrating it gives the stated parity formula. The exact-rational verifier exhaustively checks all coprime pairs through \(40\) and the floor-integral identity through \(100\). The finite replay corroborates, but the proof is analytic and quantified for all coprime positive integers.

value.rationale: Quarter flux is not an arbitrary slice: the primary source identifies it as the maximizer \(3/4\) of the incommensurate density and uses it for the commensurate Fig. 8. The theorem resolves that highlighted numerical regime for every rational arc ratio, explains the visible arithmetic dips, proves that every finite commensurate ratio lies strictly below \(3/4\), and gives the exact convergence defect for rational approximants. This is a natural spectral invariant and a structural arithmetic refinement of the source's commensurability phenomenon.
